title: From Offline Accuracy to Deployed Performance: A Four-Phase Evaluation of an Edge-Hosted Wearable Stress-Monitoring Platform
content: This paper reports a four-phase deployment evaluation of TrackWise, an edge-hosted wearable stress-monitoring application that serves a frozen Confidence-Aware Hybrid Learning (CAHIL) checkpoint through a local Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) inference service and a browser-based clinical dashboard, with no retraining performed at any stage. Phase 1 measured a mean sequential HTTP latency of 80.47 milliseconds (ms) (95th percentile [p95] = 84.86 ms), isolated route-level timing across the Machine Learning (ML)-only, Deep Learning (DL)-only, and hybrid paths, and exposed an 86.8% completion rate under 50-worker burst load, thereby identifying the serving layer as the current concurrency bottleneck. Phase 2 showed graceful degradation under progressive sensor loss on 475 real WESAD stress windows, with stress recall declining from 99.58% (95% Wilson CI: [98.48%, 99.88%]) on pristine inputs to 95.79% ([93.59%, 97.26%]) only after simultaneous removal of three of five feature modalities. Phase 3 confirmed stable 2.0 s polling cadence at the application layer. Phase 4 audited the bounded confidence transform and validated the report-export pipeline across ten sessions, with all consistency checks passing. A supplementary upload-route screening of 14 synthetic and bootstrap datasets reproduced offline aggregate predictions exactly and achieved 100% intended-label agreement on seven reliable binary controls, while transparently exposing the checkpoint’s phenotype-separation boundary on out-of-distribution profiles. Across all conditions directly tested, the deployed software preserved the dominant decision behaviour of the frozen model.
